correctness.rationale: Kallel–Sjerve Proposition 5.6 maps reduced symmetric square of a suspension to the based third finite-subset space by adjoining the basepoint and proves an integral homology isomorphism; the underlying constructions and maps are natural for based summand permutations. A reduced second symmetric power of a wedge decomposes canonically into individual reduced symmetric squares and off-diagonal smash pieces X_i smash X_j. Example 5.7 yields Sigma^(d+1) RP^(d-1) for each diagonal sphere. Its reduced integral homology has Z/2 at odd indices 1<=r<d-1 and a top Z precisely when d even. The smash factor interchange on S_i^d smash S_j^d has degree (-1)^(d^2)=(-1)^d, so the off-diagonal top lattice is the pair permutation module (d even) or wedge^2 Z^n (d odd). Naturality justifies the claimed group action on homology despite no equivariant homotopy splitting. Checked boundary d=1,d=2 and independently enumerated oriented/unoriented pair traces for all permutations n<=6.
residual_risks: Finite checks are corroborative and do not replace the all-parameter mathematical proof.

Tuffley’s graph case and later connectivity work do not determine the high-dimensional graded action. The parity-induced exterior-square sign is invisible to ordinary Betti counts. An unindexed equivariant symmetric-product computation could overlap, recorded as risk.
